# vendor

gpui-kit's code editor, forked so it can be made fast enough for large files (measured by `koyo-rs/koyo-bench`).

| Directory | Crate | Version | Upstream |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpui-base/` | `gpui-base` | 0.10.0 | [longbridge/gpui-kit](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit) `crates/base` at `f697c3133d55c64fa8a5b67926147fb3dadd276d` |
| `gpui-component/` | `gpui-component` | 0.10.0 | [longbridge/gpui-kit](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit) `crates/component` at the same commit |
| `gpui-fast/` | `gpui-fast` | 0.1.17 | the crates.io package ([longbridge/gpui-fast](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-fast)), unpacked from the `.crate` whose checksum crates.io publishes for that version (the package names no commit) |
| `gpui-fast-apple/` | `gpui-fast-apple` | 0.1.17 | the crates.io package, unpacked the same way |
| `gpui-fast-macos/` | `gpui-fast-macos` | 0.1.17 | the crates.io package ([longbridge/gpui-fast](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-fast)), unpacked the same way |

Both started as the crates.io packages unpacked as they are, `Cargo.toml` (as normalized by crates.io), `Cargo.toml.orig`, `Cargo.lock`, `.cargo_vcs_info.json` and `LICENSE-APACHE` included; each `.crate` matched the checksum in the workspace's `Cargo.lock` before it was unpacked. `git log -- koyo-rs/vendor/` shows what has changed since.

An update to newer packages is a three-way merge of every file: the base is the published file of the version vendored until then, ours the file here, theirs the new published file, each `.crate` checked against the checksum crates.io publishes for its version (`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>`). A file only upstream added or removed follows upstream, so each folder is the new package as unpacked plus the changes described here, but for what [the last update left out](#what-the-update-to-0100-and-0117-left-out).

The workspace's `Cargo.toml` (`koyo-rs/Cargo.toml`) puts them in place of the registry crates with `[patch.crates-io]`. The `gpui-kit` facade still comes from crates.io and re-exports both, so the build holds one copy of each: `cargo tree -i gpui-base` names `vendor/gpui-base`.

Neither crate is a workspace member. They keep upstream's code style and their own `[lints]` table; the workspace lint policy and `script/hygiene` cover the `koyo-rs/koyo*` crates only. Being path dependencies, their warnings aren't capped as a registry crate's are: `script/lint` holds them to rustc's and Clippy's defaults with every warning an error.

All five are licensed Apache-2.0, as is this repository; their license files (`LICENSE-APACHE`, `LICENSE`) stay with them.

## gpui-fast

GPUI's core, vendored for five changes, each marked `Koyo:`. The first, in `src/fast/splice.rs`, `src/fast/retained.rs` and `src/window.rs`: a view drawn from last frame around the views nested in it that have to be built again copies what it deferred outside them too, a bar or a popover drawn over it, unless that would replay something that changed. Upstream builds such a view again whenever it deferred anything outside them: a deferred draw is prepainted after the views around it have closed their records, so a view drawn in it is no record nested in them and is never one of the views built again, and copying the draw could replay it dirty. A chat's floating bars and its details toggle are deferred (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/chat/view/floating.rs`, `details.rs`), and each beat of a spinner on its tab or its checkout's row, 30 a second in front, built the whole shell for it.

Here the view is built again only when a draw it deferred outside them, or one deferred from that draw in turn, holds a dirty view, or what drawing it read or was hovered by has changed (`Window::deferred_outside_gaps_changed`). A draw keeps what it read and was hovered by in prepaint and paint, the views drawn in it included (`DeferredReads`, which `finish_deferred` now hands back), and each copy of it keeps that too. It keeps the retained records of the views drawn in it as well, and a copy of the draw copies them into the frame, shifted as the records nested in a subtree drawn from last frame are (`reuse_deferred_prepaint`, `reuse_deferred_paint`): a view drawn in a copied draw, a chat's composer in its floating bar, is then drawn from last frame around what is built again in it, its edge stepping, as one drawn anywhere else is.

The second, in `src/fast/dependencies.rs`: `RenderDependencies::union` merges the write marks of a recording that read nothing. Upstream returned the first side whole when the other read no entity, global or state, dropping the other's own stretch of writes: a view whose prepaint read nothing itself, while a view nested in it wrote, as an input writes its own state each time it's drawn, kept only its layout's marks, found that write foreign on the next frame and was built again. The sidebar's search field was built again at every key typed in the editor with the file tree open, and a chat's composer at each blink of its caret after the window came back in front.

The third, in `src/scene.rs`: the primitives compare by value, and `Scene::draws_like` says whether a finished scene draws what another does, which `gpui-fast-macos` uses to leave a layer that shows its frame already undrawn (below). A scene that composites a scroll layer's tiles or paints a surface never draws like another, as what those show changes with no primitive changing.

The fourth, in `src/fast/composition.rs` (`hit_test`): where a native surface is, and whether it's there at all, is asked of the composition at each hit test. Upstream notes both in the frame, once it's prepainted, and a native view that leaves the window, as a browser page's does once the frame that stopped drawing it is drawn, went on covering what was drawn in its place until the next frame: the first press there was lost (`docs/native-pages.md` 6). The frame keeps the order its surfaces are stacked in and the hitboxes on each. A test's window composes surfaces for `tests/native_surfaces.rs`, which has that press (`src/platform/test/window.rs`).

The fifth, in `src/fast/rounded_clip.rs` and `rounded_clip_scene.rs`: content fades as it reaches an edge it scrolls under (`Window::with_edge_fade`), the sidebar's rows (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/shell/sidebar/edge_fade.rs`). A clip's shape says how far in it fades from its top and its bottom, recorded, replayed, moved and compared as rounded clips are, and goes to the renderer as one more frame of metadata beside the corners'. `Window::painted_edge_fades` tells a test what a frame fades. Its pixels are in the sidebar's visual check (`sidebar-edge-fade.png`).

The published package's own tests don't build from it (the fonts, the example image and the `util_macros` crate they read aren't in it). The fourth change's test is one of Koyo's own beside them, built against the crate as it's used: `script/cargo test -p gpui-fast --test native_surfaces`. The first is tested in Koyo: `koyo-rs/koyo/src/budget/deferred.rs` checks that what is copied is drawn as the window built whole draws it, and the budgets in `koyo-rs/koyo/src/chat/tests/budget.rs` hold what a beat builds: the spinners' views, never the shell, and what a caret's blink builds, the same before the window leaves the front and after it's back.

## gpui-fast-apple

GPUI's Metal renderer, vendored for five changes, marked `Koyo:` in `src/metal_renderer.rs`, `src/shaders.metal`, `src/fast/rounded_clip.rs`, `src/fast/rounded_clip_shader.rs` and `src/fast/composition.rs`. The first: it draws a BGRA surface in the window's own frame: a simulator's or the agent desktop's picture, in the surface its host shares with the app (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/surfaces.rs`). A browser page's frame came the same way until pages became native views (`docs/native-pages.md`); what was only a page's, a picture smaller than its surface (`set_surface_picture`), has no caller now and is still in the renderer. Upstream draws only biplanar video surfaces. The renderer speaks to Metal through `objc2-metal`, as upstream's has since 0.1.17; the features of it these changes need (`objc2-io-surface` among them) are in the normalized `Cargo.toml`. `metal_renderer::set_surface_picture` says how much of the shared surface, from its top left, is the page; that part goes over the surface's bounds, and the rest of its content mask is filled by the picture's edge pixels reaching out, as while a page is laid out a frame behind a pane that grew. Rounded clips apply to it as to GPUI's other primitives. A page surface's Metal texture is made over its `IOSurface` directly, not through Core Video's texture cache, which keeps a pixel buffer until the cache is flushed; each frame keeps the pixel buffers and textures of the page surfaces it samples until the GPU has finished it (a pixel buffer marks its surface in use while it lives, which the browser host reads before painting into a surface), and no longer. Drawn with everything round it, the page can't reach the screen a frame apart from the pane's edge, which a page in a layer of its own did unless GPUI presented in Core Animation's transaction, at the cost of the window's frame rate. `build.rs` also allows the unused `stage` its shader helper module has when shaders aren't compiled ahead of time, as a path dependency's warnings aren't capped.

The second: it takes a picture of part of a frame, for the tab switcher's cards (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/shell/pictures.rs`, `docs/tab-switcher.md` 4). `metal_renderer::set_surface_capture` marks a BGRA pixel buffer as one a picture is taken into. Painted in a scene, such a buffer draws nothing; once the frame is drawn, `MetalRenderer::take_pictures` copies the frame's pixels under the buffer's bounds, as far as its content mask shows them, into a texture with mips, and draws that, shrunk, into the buffer's own `IOSurface` with the page surfaces' pipeline, whose sampler reads the mips for it (`shaders.metal`). Another buffer over the same surface then paints as any BGRA surface. A picture is taken at most every quarter second while the buffer's request stays the same, and with the next frame when it changes. Only a surface painted in the frame's own scene has its picture taken, not one inside a layer's content. A window's frames can't be read while its layer is display-only (`framebufferOnly`), which upstream leaves it outside debug builds with `test-support`: the first picture asked of a window turns that off for each of its layers, and is taken from the next frame.

A window that composes native views draws in layers, each a frame of its own with a renderer of its own (`src/fast/composition.rs`), and a picture is of all of them. The lowest layer's renderer takes it as above; the renderer of a layer over it (`MetalRenderer::draws_over`) then draws its own part of the frame over that picture, once for each the lowest takes. The layers' renderers share what they keep of the window's pictures, the last one taken and the texture a part of a frame is copied into, and one command queue, which upstream now gives every renderer on a device anyway, so the GPU draws the upper part after the lower. The native views themselves are in no frame: `metal_renderer::set_surface_pane` marks a BGRA buffer as a pane, which draws nothing in a scene and which the renderer of an upper layer fills in a picture, rounded, under its own part. Koyo's native surfaces can paint one over themselves, as its Liquid Glass does (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/native/surface.rs`). One attachment says what a surface is, a page's picture, one a picture is taken into or a pane (`Mark`), so drawing a surface reads it once.

The third: it draws a chat's backdrop, a texture Koyo made itself, which no pixel buffer can hold: the screen's picture compressed to ASTC (`koyo-rs/koyo/src/chat_backdrop/`, `docs/chat-backdrop.md` 4). `metal_renderer::register_texture` makes a texture of ASTC blocks, 4 × 4 or 8 × 8, on the system's GPU, from any thread, and gives it a number; its colours are read as they are (`ASTC_*_LDR`), as the atlas's BGRA is, not taken out of sRGB. `set_surface_backdrop` marks a BGRA pixel buffer, a pixel of it, as standing for that number and saying how it looks (`Mark::Backdrop`). Painted, the whole texture goes over the surface's bounds, as far as its content mask shows them, its rounded clips with it, drawn by a shader of its own (`backdrop_vertex`, `backdrop_fragment` in `shaders.metal`): in cells of a few pixels from the bounds' top left, each sampled at its middle and lit or not by a 4 × 4 Bayer matrix, a lit cell at its colour's full brightness and an unlit one at 8 % of it, at an opacity, fading out down the content mask. The look is Monodrive's Dither effect ([donnes/monodrive](https://github.com/donnes/monodrive), MIT, © 2026 Donald Silveira), which dithers on the CPU and fades in a pass of its own; no code of it is copied. The command buffer keeps the texture while the GPU reads it, and `release_texture` lets it go.

The fourth: the fragments that evaluate rounded clips scale what's in one that fades at its top and its bottom by how far in it is (`fast_edge_fade`), the core's edge fade (above), so it fades on glass as on anything else.

The fifth, in `src/metal_renderer.rs`: `MetalRenderer::draw` says what became of the scene (`Presented`): drawn, and into a drawable of what size; not drawn, as a display link hands the layer its drawables and the renderer holds none (`AwaitingDrawable`); or not drawn for an error it logs. A renderer a link drives never asks its layer for a drawable, so the caller keeps a scene that waits and draws it when the link hands one over (`gpui-fast-macos`, below). Upstream returns nothing and logs the frame it skips for want of a drawable. With it, `new_overlay_renderer` returns the layer it draws on beside the renderer (`src/fast/composition.rs`), which the window gives a display link of its own; upstream returns the renderer alone, whose layer is an `Option`, as a headless renderer has none.

## gpui-fast-macos

GPUI's macOS windows, vendored for changes marked `Koyo:` in `src/fast/composition.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/display_link.rs`, `src/responders.rs` and `src/gpui_macos.rs`, each for a window that composes native views (`docs/native-pages.md` 6):

- Whose a mouse button's events are (`send_window_event`). Upstream at 0.1.12 gave each drag move to whatever lay under the pointer, and kept one native view as the owner of every button until it had counted each button's release. A drag pressed on GPUI's own content, a divider beside a browser page, lost the moves made over the page; and a release the window never saw (a menu the press opened had tracked it, a drag session had taken it) left that view the owner for good, every later drag of any button going to it. Here a press owns its button: the view that took a button's press, by the button's number, gets that button's drag and release wherever the pointer is by then, a button whose press GPUI took has no entry and its events go GPUI's way, each press says anew whose its button is, and a view that leaves the window holds no press. Upstream at 0.1.17 has an answer of its own (`PointerCapture`): still one owner for every button down, GPUI or a native view, let go when a tracked button is pressed again, and GPUI's drags and releases handed to its view without `AppKit`. This crate keeps its own and leaves that out. Of upstream's it has two things: a press on the window's own chrome, its resize border or titlebar buttons, goes to `AppKit` and is nobody's, told to the app as a press on GPUI's content (`hits_window_chrome`); and where upstream lets go of its owner, as the window stops being active, starts being moved or starts a drag session, every press here is let go (`clear_pointer_capture`).
- A release GPUI never hears (`lost_releases`). GPUI's core holds a press over a native view as that view's until it hears the release, and meanwhile no press reaches GPUI's own content. GPUI's view keeps the presses it passed on and, once a move with no button down or a press while the hand's button for one is up says a press is over, tells GPUI of its release first.
- The modifiers (`send_window_event`, `route_keys`). A flags-changed event goes to GPUI's view as well whenever another view, a page's, has the keyboard: GPUI hears the modifiers only through its own view, and ⌃ let go after ⌃⇥ in a page never reached the tab switcher. GPUI already counts a change it hears twice once.
- The app's say over the keyboard (`src/responders.rs`, `docs/keyboard.md`). The app gives the windows a `Responders` (`set_responders`), which each of GPUI's windows and panels tells, on the main thread: every change of its first responder, whoever made it (`makeFirstResponder:`, overridden on both window classes, calls `AppKit`'s own and then tells the change); every key going down or up before the window delivers it to its first responder (`route_keys`, in `send_window_event`: key equivalents have been offered by then, by the application, and aren't touched); and every press of a mouse button before it's handed on, with the view under the pointer when it's in a native view of the composition (from the hit test `send_window_event` makes anyway) or nil for GPUI's own content (`tell_press`). Upstream has none of it: a native view that took the first responder on its own, as a browser page does as it opens, kept every key with GPUI never hearing of it. With no `Responders` given, the windows behave as upstream's, but for the other changes here.
- A key offered to GPUI's view while another view has the keyboard is the app's to route (`src/responders.rs`, `Responders::key_route`; `handle_key_event`; `koyoHandBackKey:`; `gpui_hears_up`). `AppKit` offers every ⌘ and ⌃ key and every function key, the arrows among them, to the window's views as a key equivalent before it delivers the key, and upstream runs everything on a key so offered, the text system too, which types into whatever has the keyboard: a left arrow in a browser page's field put a control character there and, answered as taken, never reached the page. GPUI's view now says who offers the key (`AppKit`'s pass, or the view that had the keyboard handing it back, which has a selector of its own, `koyoHandBackKey:`) and what has the keyboard, and does what the app answers: everything, its bindings alone, or nothing. The rule is the app's (`koyo-seam`, `keys::route`). A key handed back whose bindings GPUI ran has its going up told to GPUI's view too. `handle_key_event` is a function of Rust's own for it, no longer `extern "C"`. With no `Responders` given, a key is handled as upstream.
- A press that goes on to a native view is told (`src/responders.rs`, `Responders::delivered`; `send_window_event`). `pressed` tells a press before GPUI has had its say over it; `delivered` tells, with the view the press was hit-tested to, that GPUI didn't keep it and the native view is about to hear it. The app gives a browser page the keyboard by it (`docs/keyboard.md` 5): a page's view doesn't always ask for the first responder after a press.
- Native views are reordered in place (`set_composition_order`, `mount_in_order`; test `views_put_in_a_new_order_never_leave_their_parent_and_so_never_their_window`). When the order or the tree of a window's surfaces changes, upstream takes every native view out of the window and adds it back. A view that had the first responder loses it to the window, which `AppKit` does without asking, and a browser page's views hear their window lose key: Chromium stops the page being active and nothing makes it active again once back, so the page takes text with no caret until it reloads. Each view is instead put above its siblings under its parent (`addSubview:positioned:relativeTo:`), which moves it under another parent of the same window without taking it out. No view leaves the window, and the first responder stays where it was.
- A made-up release is logged (`lost_releases`): one line at `koyo::input` for each release GPUI is told of that it never heard, naming the button only.
- A key equivalent matched by its event (`handle_key_event`). Upstream lets a key press go by when it's the same keystroke as the last key equivalent, which AppKit sends first for some keys; a key a page leaves comes to GPUI as a key equivalent with no key press after it, and the next same key typed in GPUI was lost. The two are matched by the event's time too.

- A layer drawn only when what it shows changed (`src/fast/composition.rs`, `draw_composed`, `LayerState`). Upstream draws every GPUI surface of a window that composes native views at every frame. Here each layer of the window keeps the scene it last showed and the drawable size it was drawn at, and a part of a frame that draws like it (`Scene::draws_like` in `gpui-fast`) at that size isn't drawn again: the layer shows that frame still. A spinner turning under a browser page draws its own layer alone. The layer that holds the frame's whole scene, borrowed rather than replayed, is drawn each frame as before. What each layer showed is forgotten whenever the window's occlusion changes (`forget_drawn`), as macOS may let go of a hidden window's layers' contents.
- A display link for each layer over a native view (`src/display_link.rs`, `MetalFrames`, `WindowLinks`; `src/fast/composition.rs`, `start_links`, `stop_links`, `link_layer`, `layer_frame`, `end_frame`; `start_display_link`, `stop_display_link` and `metal_frame` in `src/window.rs`; tests in `src/fast/composition_tests.rs` and `src/display_link.rs`). Upstream gives only the window's own layer a `CAMetalDisplayLink`, and draws each layer over a native view into a drawable it asks Core Animation for in the frame, on the main thread (`-[CAMetalLayer nextDrawable]` under `draw_composed`). That call waits for as long as Core Animation keeps the layer's drawables, which is about a second for each drawable while the system doesn't show the layer: after the lid of a MacBook opened, or the window went to another display, three quarters of the time the main thread spent on frames went to it (the owner's app, sampled), and the window, its input and the browser pages on the same thread froze until the window was closed. Here a window's links are its own layer's and one for each layer over a native view, held together (`WindowLinks`), so no layer has a link while the window's own has none. They start together and stop together (`start_display_link`, `stop_display_link`: as the window is seen again or changes screen, and around a frame drawn at once), run and pause together, and none pauses while a layer still waits for a drawable (`MetalFrames::end_frame`). A layer that joins the window while its links run gets its link once its view is in the window, paused or running as the window's own is then (`MetalFrames::link_layer`); one that leaves loses it. A layer's renderer draws only into the drawables its link hands it, and the two are set together (`link_layer`, `stop_links`): a layer with no link, as its window's links don't run, asks for its drawables itself, and no renderer waits for a link it hasn't got. A part of a paced frame for a layer that holds no drawable is kept, the latest one winning, and drawn when the layer's link next hands it one (`LayerState::wanted`, `drawable_handed`); one drawn into a drawable from before a resize shows stretched, and is drawn again into the next. A frame drawn at once in Core Animation's transaction (`draw_in_transaction` in `src/window.rs`) stops every link of the window first, so each layer, the window's own and each over a page, asks for a drawable of its size and presents it in the transaction, as upstream's window layer does; the links start again after. Upstream set the window's layer presenting in the transaction before its link stopped. Such a frame comes only while a person drives the window's geometry: as `AppKit` asks the window's view to draw during a live resize (`display_layer`, `inLiveResize`), and as the app asks for one (`FrameAtOnce`, exported from `src/gpui_macos.rs`: Koyo's drags along a page and its fitted pop-ups, `koyo-rs/koyo/src/native/window.rs`, `docs/native-pages.md` 6), when the window is on screen and Core Animation hands drawables back at once. That is the one place left where the main thread asks Core Animation for a drawable. Every other ask of `AppKit`'s, as the view changes size when macOS fits the window to a display that just came back, or its contents are to be drawn again, wakes the window's links and their next update draws it (`draws_in_transaction` in `src/fast/composition.rs`; test `appkit_asking_outside_a_live_resize_wakes_the_links_and_draws_at_their_next_update`). Upstream drew every one at once, and its layers waited in `nextDrawable` there just as Core Animation held their drawables. Until that update the window shows the frame drawn last at the view's top left, where GPUI lays it out from, cropped or with the new edge empty, rather than stretched to the new size: the window's view and each layer over a page have their contents placed at the top left (`setLayerContentsPlacement` in `MacWindow::open` and `create_gpui_surface`), where upstream left `AppKit` stretching them. On macOS 13, which has no `CAMetalDisplayLink` and is paced by the `CVDisplayLink` (`FrameSource::DisplayLink`), every layer asks for its drawable in each frame, as upstream; Koyo is built for macOS 14 (`koyo-rs/.cargo/config.toml`).
- No frame drawn at once as the window becomes key (`window_did_change_key_status`). Upstream draws one there, in Core Animation's transaction, against tabs flickering as native tabs are switched, from the second time a window becomes key on (`activated_least_once`, which only that frame read). Koyo's windows are never tabbed: Koyo opens every window with no tabbing identifier, and each then turns `NSWindow.allowsAutomaticWindowTabbing` off (`MacWindow::open`), so macOS neither tabs them nor adds the menu items that would, and Koyo calls none of the tab methods. The frame was the window becoming key as the Mac woke or its lid opened, as Core Animation held the layers' drawables, and asked each layer for one on the main thread. A window becoming key draws at its link's next update, as any change does.
- An order that fails changes nothing (`set_composition_order`). Upstream made each new GPUI surface and put it among the window's before the rest of the order could fail (a native surface that isn't an `NSView`, a surface that couldn't be made), and kept what it had made. Here the native views' handles and every new surface are made first, and the window's surfaces change only once nothing more can fail, so a failed order leaves them as they were, and each surface it keeps has its layer's link whenever the window's links run.

## What the update to 0.10.0 and 0.1.17 left out

Upstream's code these crates don't take, each because a change described above already does its work another way:

- `gpui-base`: the reuse of a line's wrapping across widths (`src/input/editor/display_map/text_wrapper/measurements.rs` and `wrap_width.rs`, and what `text_wrapper.rs` and `wrap_map.rs` had of them). The editor's lines are wrapped where they are seen and in the background instead (`text_wrapper.rs`, `relayout_wrap` in `src/input/base/state.rs`), and an edit before the first layout still wraps the lines it touches, so upstream's test that it doesn't (`test_set_value_waits_for_the_first_layout`) is left out too. Upstream's other change to that file, a tab's indicator clipped to its tab, is here.
- `gpui-component`: the popovers upstream draws a hover and a diagnostic in (`src/input/popovers/hover_popover.rs`, `diagnostic_popover.rs`) and its placing of a menu over the caret when it doesn't fit under it (`fit_popup_origin` in `caret_anchored.rs`). The editor's cards and its own placing replace them (`cards.rs`, `diagnostic.rs`, `caret_anchored.rs`). Upstream's drawing of these popups at `POPUP_PRIORITY` is here, on the cards too.
- `gpui-fast-macos`: `src/fast/composition_capture.rs`, as the first point under [gpui-fast-macos](#gpui-fast-macos) says.

Two things upstream took over from here, and they are upstream's now: a textarea's decorations (`TextareaState::set_decorations`), which now follow edits and go with a text replaced whole, where they stayed until laid again; and `SelectableText::highlights`, beside which `with_highlights` is kept for the callers that have it.
